_help.problem: n_tasks = number of missions, n_machines = number of machines, gamma = uncertainty budget (sum of u_i <= gamma)
_help.random_instance: benchmark rounds draw d0_i ~ U(d0_range) and d_bar_i ~ U(d_bar_range); same seed -> same instances
_help.benchmark: n_rounds random instances evaluated at each gamma_values entry; reference instances are checked first
_help.milo: free pip Gurobi license is limited to 2000 vars/constraints -> MILO works up to about n_tasks=4 with 2 machines
_help.milo_exact_paper: exact replica of the paper's model (P): prune_infeasible_branches=false, enforce_non_anticipativity=true, flatten_final_phase=true; 'time' = build + ONE solve, per-first-decision solves are reported separately (root_choice_time)
_help.milo_options: enforce_non_anticipativity=false is a relaxation (upper bound); tie_tol = first-decision tie tolerance (lexicographic among ties); int_feas_tol / numeric_focus = Big-M numerical safety
_help.discrete_reference: a reference instance may give "scenarios": [[d1..dn], ...] instead of d0/d_bar/gamma -> discrete uncertainty set (MILO only)
_help.logging: trace_tree=true writes every node of both trees to the per-round log files
_help.minimax_max_candidates: minimax.max_candidates caps how many revealed-duration candidates D_F a scheduler node tries (null = all); fewer = faster, still a valid lower bound
_help.minimax_ub: ar_minimax_ub.py (upper bound, independent leaf LPs): alpha_beta=false solves every leaf LP (same value); exact_root_values=true gives the exact UB of every first decision; tie_tol = first-decision tie tolerance

reference_instances.name: example.py gap demo data (4 tasks, 2 machines)
